[ Chapter 03 — Capabilities ]

What machines can do

Six disciplines, six generative portraits — each artwork on this page is drawn live by the very kind of algorithms it describes. Move slowly. Tilt the cards.

Scroll
01 / Language

Machines that write

Trained on a trillion words of human thought, language models complete essays, contracts and confessions — one probability at a time.

02 / Vision

Machines that see

Convolutional eyes find edges in chaos: tumors in scans, pedestrians in fog, your face in a crowd of eight billion.

03 / Science

Machines that discover

AlphaFold folded two hundred million proteins — a century of biology compressed into a weekend of computation.

04 / Audio

Machines that listen

Voice becomes text, text becomes symphony. Diffusion models hallucinate frequencies no orchestra has ever played.

05 / Code

Machines that build

Copilots autocomplete software the way you finish sentences. Roughly half of all new code is now co-authored with a machine.

06 / Motion

Machines that act

From warehouse arms to humanoid prototypes, reinforcement learning turns simulation into muscle memory for machines that touch the world.

“The question of whether a computer can think is no more interesting than the question of whether a submarine can swim.” — Edsger Dijkstra
